reason: Children explain freedom from attachment at length, raising and answering objections and refuting another school's view.
Children give extended explanations of the fruits of spiritual practice and the wheel of Dharma, with scriptural citations and competing interpretations.
The first child briefly lists the six arhats but the second is a long analysis of their types, falling away and faculty transfer with doubts answered.
Children each answer a question on faculty transfer with reasons, examples and scriptural support.
Children only enumerate the nine arhats and map them onto three-by-three faculty grades without further discussion.
Children explain the two liberations and the completeness of learners and non-learners, detailing obscurations and citing a sutra.
Children explain the four kinds of path and the easy/difficult, quick/slow paths with reasons and a sutra citation.
Children map the thirty-seven factors onto ten substances and add a one-line clarification, an identification list rather than discussion.
Children are short identifications of what Dharma refers to, its two substances and a one-line gloss of its nature.
The children split a single sentence defining the unconditioned and conditioned liberation.
Children gloss successive verse lines but include argument, notably the analysis of the four alternatives of disenchantment and detachment.
Children argue why stainless patiences are views but not knowledges and which worldly wisdoms are views, with reasons.
Children set out the ten knowledges and then explain their objects at length, answering a doubt with an example.
Children explain the limits of knowing others' minds and what each practitioner knows on the path, with reasons, analogy and alternative views.
Children are one-line glosses on stainless and stained knowledge of others' minds.
Children only state in a line each the Kashmiri position and the opposing position with its proof text.
Children explain which knowledges take which as objects and why one knowledge cannot know itself, with reasons and an analogy.
The first child explains in detail which knowledges are attained and why the others are not; the second is a one-line addition.
Children explain with reasons which knowledges are obtained on the path of meditation with and without attachment.
Children are one-line statements of how many knowledges dull, sharp and transferring practitioners attain.
Children explain the nature, grounds and etymology of the ten powers at length, with reasons and a cited view.
Children list the four fearlessnesses and correlate each with a power, identification rather than discussion.
Children explain how buddhas are equal and unequal with reasons, plus an extended verse summary of their qualities.
Children are a brief statement and a list of qualities shared with others, classified by who shares them.
Children are short definitions of the four discriminating knowledges and one-line notes on their nature and grounds.
Children are brief glosses of verse lines on the six qualities' basis, nature, identification and exception.
